Artificial Intelligence for Small Business explains where AI can genuinely help with marketing, admin, customer service, planning, research and everyday operations, without pretending it will run the whole business while you drink tea and admire your own efficiency. Written in plain English for owners, freelancers, local services, consultants, creators and small teams, it focuses on practical workflows rather than technical theory. You will learn how to spot useful tasks, avoid gimmicks, improve customer communication, speed up routine work and keep control of quality. The book also covers privacy, brand voice, accuracy, cost, staff confidence and the awkward truth that some jobs still need a human being with context. It is calm, practical and sceptical in the right places. Useful AI for small business is not about chasing every shiny tool. It is about choosing a few sensible workflows and using them well.
books.summary: This book helps small business readers decide where artificial intelligence can genuinely save time and where it simply adds noise. It focuses on practical workflows across marketing, admin, customer service, research and planning, while keeping privacy, cost, brand voice and human judgement firmly in view.

books.title: AI Agents for Everyday Work
books.shortDescription: A practical guide to AI agents as controlled digital helpers for everyday work, covering tasks, boundaries, review, privacy and human judgement.
books.description: AI agents are one of the most talked-about ideas in artificial intelligence, and one of the easiest to misunderstand. This book explains them without the corporate fog. AI Agents for Everyday Work shows how digital helpers can plan tasks, use tools, draft work, organise information and support routine workflows. It also explains why they are not magic employees, why supervision matters and why a confident automated assistant can still make a glorious hash of things. Written for managers, freelancers, office workers, creators, small teams and curious professionals, the book focuses on practical everyday use: email, research, planning, admin, customer follow-up, content, meeting notes and workflow automation. It covers prompt design, task boundaries, human review, privacy, escalation, failure points and sensible adoption. The message is simple: AI agents can be useful if you keep them on a lead. The aim is not to surrender work to software, but to build controlled support systems that save time without quietly moving responsibility to a machine that cannot carry it.
books.summary: This book explains AI agents as controlled digital helpers rather than magic employees. It shows how agent-style workflows can support email, research, planning, meetings, admin and follow-up work while keeping boundaries, review, privacy and escalation rules clear.

books.title: Deepfakes, AI Scams and Synthetic Reality
books.shortDescription: A calm guide to deepfakes, AI scams, voice cloning and synthetic media, with practical verification habits for people and small organisations.
books.description: Deepfakes, fake voices, synthetic images and AI-written scams are changing how people judge what is real online. This plain-English guide explains the problem without resorting to panic theatre. Deepfakes, AI Scams and Synthetic Reality shows how artificial intelligence can be used to imitate people, manipulate media, scale fraud, fake authority and erode trust. It also explains what readers can do about it. Written for general readers, small business owners, professionals, managers, families, creators and community leaders, the book covers practical warning signs, verification habits, safer communication rules, business procedures, social media judgement and the emotional tricks behind scams. It avoids invented statistics and horror imagery. The aim is simple: help readers become harder to fool. The answer is not to distrust everything. That way lies madness and terrible group chats. The answer is to slow down, verify better, protect identity, set rules for money and sensitive requests, and understand how synthetic media changes the trust game.
books.summary: This book gives readers a calm practical framework for dealing with deepfakes, voice cloning, synthetic media and AI-enabled fraud. It focuses on verification habits, safer communication rules and everyday judgement so people and organisations become harder to fool without sliding into paranoia.

books.title: AI Literacy for the Modern Workplace
books.shortDescription: A practical workplace guide to AI literacy for managers, teams and non-technical professionals, covering prompts, policy, risk and judgement.
books.description: Many workplaces are telling people to use artificial intelligence before explaining what good use looks like. AI Literacy for the Modern Workplace fixes that gap. Written in plain English for managers, team leaders, HR, operations staff, knowledge workers and non-technical professionals, it explains the practical literacy people need to use AI sensibly at work. This is not a coding book and not a glossy innovation brochure. It covers what AI can and cannot do, how to write better prompts, how to check outputs, where human judgement matters, what data should be protected, how teams should set rules and how managers can encourage useful adoption without creating chaos. The book also deals with awkward questions: job anxiety, over-reliance, bias, accuracy, accountability, policy and the difference between productivity and simply producing more stuff. The aim is straightforward: help teams become confident, careful and useful AI users, not passengers in someone else’s software experiment.
books.summary: This book turns workplace AI literacy into a practical management and team skill. It covers prompts, output checking, privacy, policy, risk, accountability and adoption habits so non-technical professionals can use artificial intelligence with confidence rather than theatre.
